name: synced-transcript

frames.best_why: Whole player in view: header, highlighted word, both speakers and the footer bar, with no cursor covering anything.

tagline: Podcast transcript lights each spoken word inside a sliding highlight.
summary: A transcript player for dialogue: paragraphs dim ahead of the audio and brighten word by word while one grey highlight slides along the current word. A play button and thin scrub bar track the recording.
appearance: A dark rounded panel headed "Transcript" with an episode name and a small speed chip. Below, initials, speaker names and timestamps sit above grey paragraphs, one word sitting on a light grey highlight. The footer holds a round play button, a time, a thin bar and a total.
behaviour: Playing walks the highlight forward word by word, brightening spoken text and dimming what is still ahead, while the transcript scrolls itself to keep the line a third down. Clicking a word seeks there, the bar drags or steps with arrow keys, and scrolling away reveals a Back to now pill.
demo_content: Fictional podcast "Frame Rate · Episode 48" with hosts Maya and Theo talking about interface timing.
search_phrases: podcast transcript that follows the audio
words light up as they are spoken
subtitles that scroll with the voice
read along player with speed control
use_when: A podcast or interview page should let listeners read along and jump to a moment by clicking a line.
avoid_when: Playback is simulated only, so you must drive real audio through the time callback; the default script is filler text.
customise: Title, an array of speaker segments with start and end times, a duration and a time-change callback are props; speeds, word timing and colours stay in the source.
weight_why: A request-animation-frame clock while playing and a few CSS transitions; idle when paused.

a11y.note: Transport and scrubber are labelled and keyboard ready, but transcript words cannot be focused or announced as they play.

issues: A mask fades the top and bottom of the transcript, so the edge lines look washed out.
Unspoken text is a mid grey on near black, faint for long reading.
polish_why: Careful word-level sync and tidy player chrome; faint future text and faded edges cost it a little.
